title: Ethiopian Collard Greens
community: All of Ethiopia — the dark leafy green of the celebration and fasting table
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Gomen — collard greens stripped from their stems, roughly chopped, and cooked with onion, garlic, ginger, and green jalapeños. The essential green accompaniment to Doro Wat, Kitfo, and the fasting platter — its slight bitterness balances the richness of the wats.
longDesc: Gomen is as essential to the Ethiopian table as injera itself — the collard greens that appear alongside every celebration platter and every fasting spread, their slight bitterness cutting through the richness of berbere-spiced wats and the fattiness of kibbeh. Eaten alongside kitfo, they are indispensable.
ingredients: 500g collard greens (or kale) — stems removed, roughly chopped
// Fasting: use oil. Non-fasting: use kibbeh (ETH092)
steps: Blanch chopped collard greens in boiling water 3 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a wide pan.
Add garlic, ginger, and jalapeño. Cook 2 minutes.
Add blanched greens. Toss to coat.
Cook 8—10 minutes, stirring, until greens are fully wilted and fragrant.
chefTips: Blanching before the main cooking removes excess bitterness and reduces cooking time.
Strip the stems completely — they are too fibrous.
On non-fasting days, substitute kibbeh for oil — transformative.
commonMistakes: Not blanching — raw gomen takes too long and stays bitter.
cookingScience: Collard greens contain glucosinolates (compounds with powerful anti-cancer properties) and oxalic acid (which reduces mineral absorption). Blanching partially reduces the oxalic acid while retaining most of the glucosinolates. The brief subsequent sauté concentrates the flavour without destroying the nutritional compounds significantly.
sustainabilityTips: Collard greens grow year-round in Ethiopian highlands — one of the most productive and sustainable vegetables available.
servedWith: With Doro Wat (ETH061) and Kitfo (ETH029) — essential companions
healthBenefits: Very high in vitamins K, A, and C.
High calcium — important during fasting when dairy is prohibited.
culturalNote: Gomen is the green soul of Ethiopian cooking — its presence alongside Doro Wat and kitfo is as essential as the injera itself. The slight bitterness of collard greens is the Ethiopian palate's preferred green note, and a mesob platter without gomen is considered incomplete.
